title: Flat proper algebraic-space direct image preserves pseudo-coherence
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for objects with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Derived pullback and tensor use K-flat resolutions; derived direct image uses K-injective resolutions. Pseudo-coherent means etale locally represented by a bounded-above complex of finite free structure modules [def-sfb-space-pseudocoherent-complex]. Let $S$ be a scheme and $g:Y\to Z$ a flat proper morphism of finite presentation of algebraic spaces over $S$. Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed; flatness and local finite presentation are checked on etale scheme charts, and finite presentation includes quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. If $F\in D(\mathcal O_Y)$ is pseudo-coherent, then $Rg_*F$ is pseudo-coherent on $Z$. In particular, for every commutative ring $A$, every algebraic space $X$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A$, every $n\geq0$, and the projection $p:X\times_A\mathbf P^n_A\to X$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist], $Rp_*F$ is pseudo-coherent for every pseudo-coherent $F\in D(\mathcal O_{X\times_A\mathbf P^n_A})$. No Noetherian hypothesis or lower cohomological bound is required.

source.place: Tag 0CTN, lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general, pseudo-coherence conclusion; projective projection specialization used explicitly in spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tag 0CTT.

proof.text: Choose an affine etale scheme covering of $Z$. For one member $v:V\to Z$, put $Y_V=Y\times_ZV$, $g_V:Y_V\to V$, and $F_V=F|_{Y_V}$. The fibre product and covering exist by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. By [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality], $g_V$ is flat, proper and finitely presented. Since $V$ is affine, [lem-sfb-space-fp-qcqs-source] makes $Y_V$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Restriction preserves the local finite-free models in [def-sfb-space-pseudocoherent-complex]. Exact etale restriction gives $v^*Rg_*F\simeq R(g_V)_*F_V$ by [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus]. It therefore suffices to construct the required models on these charts. Until step 6 replace $(Y,Z,g,F)$ by $(Y_V,V,g_V,F_V)$.

source.place: Tag 0CTN, lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general, expanded through Tag 0CTL, lemma-base-change-tensor-pseudo-coherent, with coefficient complex O_Y[0].

proof.text: The morphism $g$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and its base is now affine. Choose $N\geq1$ from [lem-sfb-space-derived-pushforward-upper-bound]. Fix any integer $m$ and set $a=m-N-1$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-pseudocoherent-perfect-approximation] on the qcqs space $Y$: it gives $F\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$, a perfect $P$, and a distinguished triangle $P\xrightarrow{u}F\to C\to P[1]$ in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$, with $H^i(u)$ an isomorphism for $i>a$ and $H^a(u)$ surjective. The long exact sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] gives $H^i(C)=0$ for $i\geq a$: in degree $a$ use that surjection and the injection in degree $a+1$, and in higher degrees use both adjacent isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0CTN, lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general, expanded through Tag 0CTL, lemma-base-change-tensor-pseudo-coherent, with coefficient complex O_Y[0].

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-proper-support-tensor-perfect] with $E=P$ and $G^\bullet=\mathcal O_Y[0]$. This is bounded; its degree-zero term is quasi-coherent and finitely presented, with presentation $0\to\mathcal O_Y\xrightarrow{1}\mathcal O_Y\to0$. To check relative flatness use [lem-sfb-space-module-flat-chart-test]: on any etale scheme atlas $U\to Y$, the corresponding module is $\mathcal O_U$, and its stalk is flat over the base stalk since $U\to Z$ is flat by [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test] and [def-weil-flat-morphism]. The annihilator of $\mathcal O_Y$ is zero, so its support subspace is $Y$, proper over $Z$. Every zero term has empty support, proper by [lem-sfb-space-proper-support-closed-operations] (the empty union). Thus $Rg_*(P\otimes^L\mathcal O_Y[0])$ is perfect. On a K-flat representative $Q$ of $P$, the termwise maps $Q^i\otimes\mathcal O_Y\to Q^i$, $q\otimes r\mapsto rq$, commute with differentials and are inverse to $q\mapsto q\otimes1$. Hence $P\otimes^L\mathcal O_Y[0]\simeq P$, and $Rg_*P$ is perfect.

source.place: Tag 0CTN, lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general, expanded through Tag 0CTL, lemma-base-change-tensor-pseudo-coherent, with coefficient complex O_Y[0].

proof.text: Apply the upper-bound theorem of step 2 to $C$ with $b=a-1$. It gives $H^j(Rg_*C)=0$ for $j\geq a-1+N=m-2$. The canonical direct image is additive and K-injective-derived [def-sfb-space-derived-module-calculus]; [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated] therefore gives a distinguished triangle $Rg_*P\to Rg_*F\to Rg_*C\to(Rg_*P)[1]$. For $i\geq m$, both $H^{i-1}(Rg_*C)$ and $H^i(Rg_*C)$ vanish. Its long exact sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] makes $H^i(Rg_*u)$ an isomorphism for every $i\geq m$. This calculation uses only an upper bound on $C$, never a lower bound.

source.place: Tag 0CTN, lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general, expanded through Tag 0CTL, lemma-base-change-tensor-pseudo-coherent, with coefficient complex O_Y[0].

proof.text: Put $K=Rg_*F$. By [lem-sfb-space-derived-pushforward-coproducts], $K$ has quasi-coherent cohomology. Since $Z$ is a scheme, [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence] supplies $K_0\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{Z,\mathrm{Zar}})$ with $\epsilon_Z^*K_0\simeq K$. For each $m$, the perfect object $Rg_*P$ of step 3 has local strictly perfect models; composing these with $Rg_*u$ and using step 4 gives isomorphisms above $m$ and a surjection in degree $m$. These are precisely the small-etale $m$-pseudo-coherence witnesses in [lem-sfb-etale-pseudocoherence-descent]. That lemma implies that $K_0$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent on the Zariski site. This holds for every integer $m$, so [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex] gives local bounded-above finite-free models for $K_0$. Exact $\epsilon_Z^*$ takes such a model to a finite-free model for $K$ on the small etale site, identifying the structure modules by [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence].

source.place: Tag 0CTN, lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general, expanded through Tag 0CTL, lemma-base-change-tensor-pseudo-coherent, with coefficient complex O_Y[0].

proof.text: Return to the original space $Z$. The isomorphisms of step 1 and models of step 5 give derived finite-free models on an etale covering, and on further slice restrictions of that covering. To meet the representative formulation of [def-sfb-space-pseudocoherent-complex], choose one K-injective representative $I$ of $Rg_*F$ on the small ringed model using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Its restrictions remain K-injective by [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized]. Each derived isomorphism from a local finite-free complex $L$ to $I|_U$ is represented by a chain map by [lem-sc-kinjective-quasi-iso-comparison]; that map is a quasi-isomorphism since its image in the derived category is invertible. Thus all local models map into the single representative $I$. For any other etale site object, pull back the covering and these chain maps; exact slice restriction [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus] preserves their quasi-isomorphisms. This is exactly the covering-sieve condition of the definition. Hence $Rg_*F$ is pseudo-coherent.

source.place: Tag 0CTN, lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general, expanded through Tag 0CTL, lemma-base-change-tensor-pseudo-coherent, with coefficient complex O_Y[0].

proof.text: For the projective projection, first work over an affine etale chart $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$. Identify polynomial Proj with base-change projective space by [lem-trf-free-projective-bundle-base-change-space]. Then the fibre product of $X\times_A\mathbf P^n_A$ with $V$ is $\mathbf P^n_R$ by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-pullback]. Its projection $p_V$ is proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]. By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts], its $n+1$ standard affine opens have rings $R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$. Each projection from a chart is flat by [lem-nagata-polynomial-projection-flat]. Flatness is local for the jointly surjective open, hence etale, cover by [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties], so $p_V$ is flat. On each chart this polynomial algebra has $n$ generators and zero relations; [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] therefore makes $p_V$ locally of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 0CTT, lemma-characterize-pseudo-coherent, projective projection; constructions.tex Tags 01NF (definition-projective-space), 01NG (lemma-standard-covering-projective-space); Morphisms Tags 01U5 and 01TP.

proof.text: Properness makes $p_V$ quasi-compact and separated. Since its base is affine, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] makes $\mathbf P^n_R$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Then [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) makes $p_V$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Together with the local finite presentation in step 7 this is finite presentation in [def-pc-morphism-conventions]. These scheme properties of $p_V$ are the algebraic-space properties required in steps 1--6: flatness and local finite presentation by the scheme clause of [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test], and properness by the scheme agreement recorded in [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Apply steps 1--6 to $p_V$ and the restricted pseudo-coherent $F$. It follows that $R(p_V)_*(F|_{\mathbf P^n_R})$ is pseudo-coherent. The exact etale base-change comparison [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus] identifies this with $(Rp_*F)|_V$. The models on all such $V$ give pseudo-coherence on $X$ by the same covering and representative argument of step 6. For $n=0$ there is one affine chart with ring $R$ and the argument is unchanged; empty charts and the zero ring cause no exception.
